questions.title: Question 1: Energy Source
questions.text: What naturally energizes and motivates you most?

options.A: Achieving specific goals and seeing measurable progress toward objectives
options.B: Learning new things and expanding your knowledge or skills
options.C: Making a positive difference in people's lives or contributing to something meaningful
options.D: Experiencing variety, excitement, and new challenges regularly

questions.title: Question 2: Work Rhythm Preference
questions.text: Your ideal work rhythm involves:

options.A: Steady, consistent progress with clear milestones and regular achievements
options.B: Deep focus periods alternating with time for reflection and skill development
options.C: Collaborative work that creates value for others and builds relationships
options.D: Dynamic, varied activities with frequent changes and new experiences

questions.title: Question 3: Feedback and Recognition
questions.text: You feel most motivated by feedback that:

options.A: Shows concrete results and measurable improvements in performance
options.B: Acknowledges your expertise, learning progress, and skill development
options.C: Recognizes your positive impact on others and contribution to the team
options.D: Celebrates your adaptability, creativity, and ability to handle challenges

questions.title: Question 4: Challenge Response
questions.text: When faced with a difficult task, you're most energized when:

options.A: You can break it into clear steps with specific outcomes to achieve
options.B: You can research, analyze, and develop expertise to master it completely
options.C: You can work with others and see how success will benefit people
options.D: It offers something new and different from your usual routine

questions.title: Question 5: Success Definition
questions.text: You feel most successful when:

options.A: You've accomplished your goals and can see tangible results from your efforts
options.B: You've gained mastery or deep understanding in an area that interests you
options.C: You've helped others succeed or contributed to something larger than yourself
options.D: You've overcome challenges and experienced growth through new experiences

questions.title: Question 6: Motivation Drivers
questions.text: What drives you to put in extra effort?

options.A: The satisfaction of completing projects and achieving targets
options.B: The opportunity to become an expert or learn something fascinating
options.C: The chance to make a meaningful impact on others or society
options.D: The excitement of tackling something new and unpredictable

questions.title: Question 7: Energy Drain
questions.text: You feel most drained and unmotivated when:

options.A: Progress is unclear or you can't see concrete results from your work
options.B: Work is repetitive with no opportunity to learn or develop skills
options.C: Your work feels meaningless or disconnected from helping others
options.D: You're stuck in routine tasks with no variety or new challenges

questions.title: Question 8: Team Dynamics
questions.text: In team settings, you're most energized when:

options.A: The team has clear objectives and everyone is working toward specific results
options.B: You can contribute your expertise and learn from others' knowledge
options.C: There's strong collaboration and mutual support among team members
options.D: The team tackles diverse projects and adapts quickly to changing needs

questions.title: Question 9: Long-term Engagement
questions.text: For long-term motivation, you need:

options.A: Clear career progression with achievable goals and visible advancement
options.B: Continuous opportunities to develop expertise and expand your capabilities
options.C: Work that aligns with your values and creates positive impact
options.D: Regular changes in responsibilities, projects, or work environment

questions.title: Question 10: Decision-Making Energy
questions.text: You're most motivated to make decisions when:

options.A: You can evaluate options based on likely outcomes and results
options.B: You have sufficient information and expertise to make an informed choice
options.C: The decision will positively affect people you care about
options.D: The decision opens up new possibilities and adventures

questions.title: Question 11: Stress and Pressure
questions.text: Under pressure, you maintain energy best when:

options.A: You can focus on specific deliverables and track progress toward completion
options.B: You can apply your knowledge and skills to solve the problem systematically
options.C: You remember how your work serves others and contributes to something important
options.D: You can approach the situation creatively and try different solutions

questions.title: Question 12: Learning Motivation
questions.text: You're most motivated to learn when:

options.A: The learning will help you achieve specific goals or improve performance
options.B: The subject matter is intellectually stimulating and builds expertise
options.C: The knowledge will help you better serve others or make a difference
options.D: The learning involves new experiences and keeps things interesting

questions.title: Question 13: Autonomy and Control
questions.text: You feel most energized when you have:

options.A: Clear expectations but freedom in how you achieve your goals
options.B: Time and resources to pursue mastery in areas of interest
options.C: Opportunities to collaborate while contributing your unique strengths
options.D: Flexibility to adapt your approach and try new methods

questions.title: Question 14: Recognition Preferences
questions.text: You prefer recognition that:

options.A: Highlights specific achievements and measurable contributions
options.B: Acknowledges your expertise, knowledge, and professional growth
options.C: Emphasizes your positive impact on others and team contribution
options.D: Celebrates your adaptability, innovation, and willingness to take on challenges

questions.title: Question 15: Work Environment Energy
questions.text: You thrive in environments that:

options.A: Have clear structures, expectations, and opportunities for advancement
options.B: Value expertise, provide learning resources, and encourage skill development
options.C: Emphasize collaboration, shared purpose, and positive impact
options.D: Offer variety, flexibility, and opportunities for new experiences

questions.title: Question 16: Motivation Sustainability
questions.text: Your motivation stays high when:

options.A: You can see steady progress and regular accomplishments
options.B: You're continuously growing and developing new capabilities
options.C: Your work connects to your values and benefits others
options.D: You face new challenges and have opportunities for change

questions.title: Question 17: Goal Setting Energy
questions.text: You're most motivated by goals that are:

options.A: Specific, measurable, and have clear deadlines for achievement
options.B: Focused on skill development, learning, or expertise building
options.C: Connected to helping others or contributing to meaningful causes
options.D: Flexible, exciting, and offer opportunities for creative approaches

questions.title: Question 18: Collaboration Style
questions.text: In collaborative work, you're energized when:

options.A: Everyone has clear roles and the team is focused on achieving results
options.B: You can share knowledge and learn from others' expertise
options.C: There's mutual support and the work benefits everyone involved
options.D: The collaboration brings together diverse perspectives and approaches

questions.title: Question 19: Change Response
questions.text: Your energy level with organizational change:

options.A: Increases when change leads to clearer goals and better results
options.B: Increases when change provides learning opportunities and skill development
options.C: Increases when change improves conditions for people and creates positive impact
options.D: Increases when change brings variety and new challenges

questions.title: Question 20: Legacy and Impact
questions.text: You're most motivated by the prospect of:

options.A: Building a track record of consistent achievement and successful results
options.B: Becoming recognized as an expert or thought leader in your field
options.C: Making a lasting positive difference in people's lives or society
options.D: Having diverse experiences and adapting successfully to whatever comes

A.name: Goal-Oriented Achiever
A.summary: You are energized by clear goals, measurable progress, and achieving specific outcomes. You like steady progress and milestones.
scoring_bullets: Goal Completion: Deeply motivated by reaching specific targets and objectives
Progress Visibility: Need to see measurable advancement and concrete results
Performance Excellence: Driven by the satisfaction of high performance and success
Competitive Edge: Energized by challenges that test and prove capabilities

B.name: Hands-On Creator
B.summary: You are motivated by building, creating, and making things. You prefer learning by doing and seeing tangible results.
scoring_bullets: Skill Development: Deeply motivated by becoming excellent at meaningful work
Knowledge Acquisition: Energized by learning new concepts and expanding understanding
Expertise Building: Driven by the journey toward mastery and professional growth
Intellectual Challenge: Motivated by complex problems that require deep thinking

C.name: Knowledge Seeker
C.summary: You are driven by understanding concepts deeply and exploring ideas. You value insight and mastery of subject matter.
scoring_bullets: Meaningful Impact: Deeply motivated by work that makes a positive difference
Value Alignment: Energized when work connects to personal values and beliefs
Service to Others: Driven by opportunities to help, support, and contribute to others
Legacy Building: Motivated by creating lasting positive change

D.name: Balanced Innovator
D.summary: You combine theory and practice. You like both understanding why and applying how, with flexibility in your approach.
scoring_bullets: Novelty and Change: Deeply motivated by new experiences and fresh challenges
Stimulation and Excitement: Energized by dynamic, unpredictable environments
Flexibility and Autonomy: Driven by freedom to adapt and try different approaches
Growth Through Challenge: Motivated by overcoming obstacles and expanding comfort zones

scoring_intro: Scoring Guide: How to Calculate Your Score: Step 1: Count your responses for each letter: Count all your A responses (Achievement-Driven), B (Mastery-Oriented), C (Purpose-Driven), D (Variety-Seeking). Step 2: Determine your engagement pattern based on your highest scores.
mixed_results: Dual Engagement Pattern (Two Dominant Styles): Score Range 8–12 in two categories, others below 6. e.g. High A + High B: Achievement-Mastery (Expert Achiever); High A + High C: Achievement-Purpose (Mission-Focused Achiever); High B + High C: Mastery-Purpose (Meaningful Expert); High C + High D: Purpose-Variety (Flexible Contributor). Balanced Engagement Pattern: 6–10 across three or more categories. Multi-Modal Engagement: Relatively even scores across all categories (5–8 in each).
